id: title:gantoine:run the full backend matrices when the selector has no durations

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a duration tracking field and a runtime validation check to selection fixtures, potentially improving scheduling or resource allocation reliability.
review.reason: The chunk adds a new field 'total_seconds' to selection fixtures and includes a runtime check to reject selections where this duration is not greater than zero. This establishes a new data point and a guard against invalid scheduling inputs.
review.uncertainty: The specific PostHog product or operational mechanism this selection scheduling supports is not identified in the provided observations; the connection is inferred rather than demonstrated. No tests or implementation checks are shown to demonstrate the actual benefit of this change.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains only test and implementation changes. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds a new field 'total_seconds' to the selection fixture and its usage, and adds a runtime check for this field.
observations.posthog_connection: This field appears to represent a duration metric for the selection, possibly the total time allocated or consumed, while selected_seconds and skipped_seconds represent subsets. This could relate to scheduling or resource allocation for CI execution.

observations.behavior: Adds a new test case and an implementation check: if total_seconds is not greater than 0, the selection is treated as invalid and a fallback is used.
observations.code_quote: [{ selection: selectionFixture({ durations: { total_seconds: 0, selected_seconds: 0, skipped_seconds: 0 } }) }, 'no_durations'],
observations.posthog_connection: This could help prevent execution of selections with zero or missing duration, potentially avoiding scheduling errors or resource contention in CI.

observations.behavior: Updates the selection fixture to include total_seconds alongside selected_seconds_by_segment.
observations.code_quote: durations: { total_seconds: 90000, selected_seconds_by_segment: { core: 5000, poe: 0, temporal: 900 } },
